profile.title: About the university
profile.hint: Everything else starts from this data: the name sits at the top for everyone who signs in, and the time zone decides when a class begins. Check and confirm — if something is wrong, write to us, we edit the details.

faculties.title: Faculties
faculties.hint: A faculty is the top level of the structure: groups, deans and access rights all rest on it. Without faculties no further step can be completed.

specialties.title: Specialities
specialties.hint: The list a student picks their speciality from in their profile. Start with the main ones — you can add the rest later in the specialities section.

groups.title: Groups
groups.hint: A group is what the schedule, the gradebook and the chats attach to. A student is invited into a group, not into the university at large, so without groups no student can be invited.

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.hint: Rooms are needed by the schedule and by the printed QR above the door: a student scans the code and sees what is happening here right now.

terms.title: Academic year
terms.hint: A term sets the boundaries of the study period. Without one you cannot build a schedule or open the gradebook: a class has nowhere to land in time.

subjects.title: Subjects
subjects.hint: The university's shared list of disciplines — courses and the schedule are assembled from it. Start with the main ones and add more as you build the schedule.

deans.title: Deans
deans.hint: This is where the chain starts: you invite the dean, the dean invites the monitors and the students. That way each next person comes from whoever is responsible for them, not from a general list. The invite link appears right after you create it.

launch.title: Go live
launch.hint: Until the university goes live it exists but does not work. Going live opens the platform to everyone you have invited.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: StudentHub is a closed platform your university grants access to by invitation. This page explains what data is processed, why, and who can see it.

sections.heading: 1. Who processes your data
sections.body: The controller of your personal data is the university that issued your invitation. StudentHub processes data on its instructions and only to the extent the platform needs to work.

sections.heading: 2. What data is processed
sections.body: Account data: first and last name, email, username, role, faculty and group. Profile: photo, contacts and any details you fill in yourself. Academic data: schedule, applications, grades, attendance, submitted work and documents. Content you publish: posts, comments, messages and files. Technical data: connection address, device and browser type, sign-in times.

sections.heading: 3. Why it is needed
sections.body: Your data is used to give you access to academic services, show your schedule and grades, process applications, enable communication inside the university, protect your account from unauthorised sign-ins, and handle reports of misconduct.

sections.heading: 4. Who can see your data
sections.body: You control profile visibility in your settings. Teachers, the group leader and the dean's office see academic data within their groups and courses. University administrators see the accounts of their own institution. Platform staff access data only for technical support and incident handling.

sections.heading: 5. Storage and protection
sections.body: Your password is stored only as an irreversible hash — it cannot be recovered, which is why we never ask for it. Connections are protected by HTTPS and two-factor authentication is available for your account. Data is kept while your university account is active and is deleted or anonymised under the university's rules once it is closed.

sections.heading: 6. Your rights
sections.body: You can view and correct your profile data, limit its visibility, hide your email and delete your own publications. Requests to export, correct or erase data are submitted to your university administrator or the dean's office.

sections.heading: 7. Cookies and browser storage
sections.body: We use technical cookies for the sign-in session and browser local storage for interface settings and drafts. There are no advertising or third-party trackers on the platform, and no data is shared with ad networks.

sections.heading: 8. Minors
sections.body: If you are under 18, consent to the processing of personal data is given on your behalf by a legal representative — a parent or guardian; consent given by a minor alone has no legal force. The university collects that consent at enrolment, together with the rest of the documents; the platform works with the data only to the extent the university passed it on.

sections.heading: 9. Changes to this policy
sections.body: We announce changes inside the platform. By continuing to use StudentHub after an update, you accept the new version.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms describe the rules for using StudentHub. By starting to work in the platform, you accept them.

sections.heading: 1. General provisions
sections.body: Access to the platform is granted by your university. Registration is only possible with a personal invitation; the invitation link must not be passed on to anyone else. If you are under 18, these terms are accepted on your behalf by your legal representative.

sections.heading: 2. Your account
sections.body: An account belongs to one person. Do not share your login, password or confirmation codes with third parties: everything done under your account is considered done by you. If you suspect someone else has gained access, change your password immediately and notify your university administrator.

sections.heading: 3. Rules of conduct
sections.body: Insults, harassment and threats, incitement of hatred, spam and bulk messaging, adult material, publishing someone else's personal data without consent, impersonating another person or staff member, and attempts to bypass access restrictions are all prohibited.

sections.heading: 4. Your content
sections.body: You keep the rights to the material you publish. By publishing content you allow the platform to store it and show it to the participants it is addressed to. You are responsible for the legality of what you publish and for holding the rights to the material you use.

sections.heading: 5. Academic integrity
sections.body: Learning materials, submitted work and grades in the platform belong to your university's academic process. Cheating, passing off someone else's work as your own and distributing closed assessment materials are judged under the university's rules.

sections.heading: 6. Moderation
sections.body: Violations can be reported through the built-in form. Moderators and the university administration may hide material, restrict access to individual features or block an account. Decisions can be appealed through the dean's office.

sections.heading: 7. Service availability
sections.body: The platform may be temporarily unavailable due to maintenance or failures. We work to keep such interruptions short, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted operation and are not liable for consequences caused by circumstances beyond our control.

sections.heading: 8. Changes and termination of access
sections.body: These terms may be updated; we announce changes inside the platform. Access ends on expulsion, termination of employment, or by decision of the university. Data is processed afterwards under the university's rules.
